top.title: Wild beat Bruins 6-2 behind two goals from Ryan Hartman, extending road winning streak to 8 games
top.description: Nov 14, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Minnesota Wild left wing Kirill Kaprizov (97) congratulates right wing Ryan Hartman (38) after scoring a goal during the second period against the Boston Bruins at TD Garden. Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect BOSTON — Ryan Hartman and Danila Yurov scored two goals each, Jesper Wallstedt stopped 30 shots, and the Minnesota Wild beat the Boston Bruins 6-2 on Saturday night to extend their road winning streak to eight games. Kirill Kaprizov extended his point streak to 11 games (six goals, 14 assists) with two assists for the West-leading Wild, who have earned at least a point in 11 straight games (9-0-2). Quinn Hughes and Blake Coleman scored 67 seconds apart in the opening two minutes of the second period for Minnesota, which cruised to its NHL-best 10th road victory. Yurov scored both of his in the third period, the second an empty-netter. David Pastrnak and Fraser Minten scored for Boston, which lost its second straight home game after winning seven in a row at TD Garden. Both losses came wearing their new mostly brown “varsity jerseys” with bright yellow numbers, trim and helmets that they debuted Thursday. After getting pulled in Boston’s lopsided loss at home against Montreal Thursday — its first at home since Oct. 5 — Jeremy Swayman started and made 19 saves. Hartman’s first came on a wrister from the left circle that beat Swayman inside the far post, making it 1-0 at 6:54 of the opening period. Hughes slipped a wrister past Swayman 53 seconds into the middle period and Coleman’s slap shot from the point found its way past a few bodies and into the net, making it 3-0. Minten’s power-play goal came at 8:45 but Hartman’s second took away Boston’s brief momentum 75 seconds later. The Wild won the first meeting of the season , 4-1, at home on Oct. 3 when Kaprizov scored two goals. The teams entered tied with the NHL’s second-best goal differential (plus-24) behind Carolina.

top.title: Seahawks avoid travel issues for Raiders game following nationwide ground stop
top.description: It’s been a hectic weekend for airline travel after apparent equipment issues resulted in a nationwide ground stop on Friday. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) did lift the order after four hours, but the resulting chaos was thousands of canceled and rescheduled flights, which continued into Saturday. Luckily, while college sports were significantly impacted by the sudden travel issues, the Seattle Seahawks were able to head to Las Vegas to take on the Raiders as originally scheduled. The Seahawks are en route to Las Vegas right now as planned, so no changes to their travel schedule. — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) November 14, 2026 It sure helps to have a charter flight in this scenario. For shorter trips like Seattle to Las Vegas, the Seahawks will typically travel on a Saturday, whereas cross-country trips like their Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders have involved Friday departures. The NFL is probably fortunate that not a single Week 10 Sunday matchup has a Pacific Time Zone team playing in the Eastern Time Zone (or vice versa). College football and basketball games were rescheduled throughout the country as a result of Friday’s outage, with the Washington Huskies men’s basketball matchup with Utah postponed outright to December due to additional travel problems . Huskies football did fly to Michigan on Friday night but still had their kickoff against Michigan State moved back by an hour. The NFL didn’t come away from the travel nightmare unscathed, as several games will have makeshift officiating crews. Side judge Don Willard will be the head referee for the Miami Dolphins and Indianapolis Colts at 10 am PT, then drive to Cincinnati to ref the Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football at 5:20 pm PT. Unfortunately, some fans hoping to go to Vegas for a weekend to catch some Seahawks football had their dreams dashed, as we documented on Friday .

top.title: Real Madrid tipped to complete first signing of 2027 for just €9 million
top.description: Real Madrid tipped to complete first signing of 2027 for just €9 million Real Madrid are already looking towards the summer 2027 transfer window as the club seek to strengthen the squad at Jose Mourinho’s disposal. The signings they made in 2026 have worked out very well so far, with each player finding a way to contribute to Mourinho’s team. One player who could feature prominently in their 2027 plans is Jacobo Ramon, who has developed remarkably since leaving the Santiago Bernabeu for Como in 2025. Real Madrid planning €9 million move for Jacobo Ramon According to journalist Miguel Serrano, speaking on his YouTube channel, Los Blancos are increasingly convinced that they should bring the academy graduate back next summer. “Real Madrid are clear that they have to bring Jacobo back,” Serrano explained, suggesting that the defender could become the club’s first signing ahead of the 2027/28 campaign (h/t Defensa Central ). Madrid possess a buy-back option worth approximately €9 million, having initially sold the youngster to Como for €2.5 million. Real Madrid want to bring back Jacobo Ramon to the club. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Serrano admitted that his opinion of Ramon has changed considerably since watching him against Leganes during Carlo Ancelotti’s final season. “He has grown under Fabregas, become an undisputed starter and is now a senior international,” the journalist explained. The 21-year-old’s performances in Italy have established him as one of the most promising young defenders in European football. Mourinho could have room for another centre-back Ramon could return as the fourth-choice centre-back, competing for minutes alongside Dean Huijsen, Ibrahima Konate and Eder Militao. Antonio Rudiger is also expected to stay for another season, but considering his age, he is unlikely to feature regularly for the team. Ramon could take up Rudiger’s place in the squad. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Ramon could come in and provide Mourinho with a high-quality option in a position where the right balance is always crucial. Alternatively, should the club feel they do not have space in their squad, they could buy him and then sell him back to Como. This is a trick Los Blancos pulled off quite neatly with Nico Paz this past summer, and they can do the same with Ramon. Regardless, Real Madrid signing Ramon seems like a given at this stage, and it remains to be seen how things play out.

top.title: The relentless rise of Jason Cundy: How a forgotten footballer became UK sports radio's most popular wind-up merchant
top.description: Jason Cundy GFX - GOAL/talkSPORT The 56-year-old former Chelsea defender is on a 'generational run', going viral on a near-weekly basis for his antics on talkSPORT Younger football fans could be forgiven for not having heard of Jason Cundy until a few years ago. A playing career that had so much promise would drift into relative obscurity after his time at Chelsea and Tottenham in the 90s, and he was even forced into early retirement. Now, though, he is going viral across social media on a near-weekly basis for his on-air antics. Cundy is a talkSPORT stalwart after more than 20 years with the radio station, but his emergence as a master wind-up merchant has seen his popularity soar. In fact, the 56-year-old's 'generational run' means there there is an argument he should be sweeping sports broadcasting awards in 2026. Chelsea, survival & early retirement Cundy started his career at Chelsea before going on to play for Tottenham, but his playing days were hampered by a series of health problems While he is now arguably more synonymous with being a broadcaster after more than 20 years in the business, Cundy actually enjoyed a top-level professional playing career that incorporated spells at Chelsea and, ironically, their London rivals Tottenham, whom he now spends a significant chunk of his time tearing into. A lifelong Chelsea fan who used to watch the Blues at Stamford Bridge as a boy, the tough-tackling centre-back came through the club's academy in the 80s, earning their Young Player of the Year award in 1987. He spent four years in the first team in west London before being sold to Spurs in 1992. Hampered by persistent fitness issues throughout his career, Cundy was forced to be patient for opportunities at White Hart Lane and headed on various loans before permanent spells with Ipswich Town and Portsmouth. It was during his time with the latter that the defender was diagnosed with testicular cancer in early 1997, undergoing surgery to remove one of his testicles and eventually making a full recovery, returning to the pitch later that year. However, his playing days would be curtailed three years later. In December 2000, aged just 31, he was forced to retire on medical advice following a serious knee injury that he had actually suffered in training when he was still an Ipswich player, with his final appearance coming almost a year prior on Boxing Day 1999. "I haven't put my boots on since that game at Swindon," Cundy said at the time. "I cleaned them after the game, put them in the boot of my car - and they've been there ever since. It's a sad day. I'm now an ex-pro footballer. When I signed as a 17-year-old for Chelsea, I never imagined it would ever come to this." top.title: Bundesliga defender not a viable option for Barcelona despite recent links – report
top.description: Bundesliga defender not a viable option for Barcelona despite recent links – report Last week, it was reported that Jonathan Tah has emerged as a potential candidate for Barcelona as they look to shore up their ranks in the defensive unit in January. The club have struggled with injuries in the defensive department, with the likes of Eric Garcia, Andreas Christensen, Jules Kounde, and Xavi Espart all picking up injuries at some form or the other. This has led Barcelona to reportedly consider a move for Bayern Munich star Tah, who is a key defender for both his club and country. Tah not an option for Barcelona Jonathan Tah is a key player for German national team. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) However, a recent report from Diario SPORT has now clarified that Tah is not a serious option for Barcelona. This is largely because Bayern Munich are not willing to consider the sale of the German international, while the player himself is not too keen on leaving the club either. Therefore, a Barcelona move for Tah has been practically ruled out, even though the club are interested in acquiring the services of the former Bayer Leverkusen star. It must be noted that Barça were one of the contenders to sign Tah when he had decided to run out his contract at Leverkusen in 2025. Ultimately, Bayern Munich won the race to his signature. No change of air required Tah believes Bayern is the place to be. (Photo by Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images) The report points out that Barcelona do have an excellent relationship with Tah’s agent, Pini Zahavi. The Israeli agent is the representative of Hansi Flick and shares a good bond with Joan Laporta, having previously helped the club sign Robert Lewandowski as well. However, Tah is simply not willing to leave Bayern Munich, having already established himself as a key player at the back, with 67 appearances in all competitions since joining the club. Now a regular in the German team as well, Tah is currently at the peak of his powers and believes Bayern is the place to be. Barcelona, for their part, are aware of Tah’s lack of desire to switch clubs and therefore, are likely to shift their focus onto other potential targets in the market.

top.title: Terry Butcher compares Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane to 1966 World Cup hero Bobby Moore and backs striker to lead England to Euro 2028 glory
top.description: England v Croatia - UEFA Nations League 2026/27 Group A3 MD5 - Getty Images Sport Former England captain Terry Butcher has likened Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane to 1966 World Cup-winning skipper Bobby Moore after the striker broke the nation's all-time appearance record. Following Thursday's milestone outing against Croatia at Wembley, the ex-defender has backed the forward to lead the Three Lions to Euro 2028 glory. Former skipper hails record-breaking striker Butcher believes the 33-year-old striker commands the same respect as England's only World Cup-winning captain and can end the country's major trophy wait on home soil in two years' time. Present at Wembley on Thursday to collect his own legacy cap, the former centre-back watched Kane celebrate his recent Ballon d'Or triumph by becoming England's most-capped men's player . The forward marked the occasion by converting the winning penalty in a 2-1 UEFA Nations League victory over Croatia. Model professional leads by example Speaking to the Press Association about Kane's leadership and longevity ahead of the 2028 finals co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland from June 9 to July 9, Butcher said: "I think he is terrific. He's playing some of the best football of his career now. He's relaxed, he's fit, he looks strong, he's got a fantastic attitude. He's looked after by really nice people. "He lives the right way, behaves the right way, plays the right way. He's a model professional. For me, he just resembles Bobby Moore in terms of how people look up to him. "He is a different type of player to me, he's a striker, and I was a centre back and most people prefer someone at the back or in midfield to be captain, but he leads by example. He does the right things and he's someone that has a strong mentality. He's someone that wants it and well respected. "He's still got life in him, we still want him to get more caps, we still want him to get more goals. The World Cup might be just too far away, but the Euros are certainly within the realms of possibility that he can captain England there. I certainly hope so." Home tournament offers golden opportunity After reaching the last two European Championship finals and claiming bronze at this summer's World Cup - their third semi-final since 1966 following the 1990 run when Butcher wore the armband - the ex-defender feels only a mental barrier remains: "It is a mentality in terms of we've been there before and we haven't got over, but you've got to just dismiss that. "There's a big hump or a big chasm, once you get over that, you're on the other side, it's like, 'wow, this is the promised land.' But I think I think they're well placed [to win it]. It'd be great to be at home, in front of our home crowd and it's perfectly set up for us to do that now. We've got to take advantage of that." top.title: Georgia Tech WR coach DeAndre Hopkins has perfect reaction to beating alma mater Clemson
top.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Georgia Tech WR coach DeAndre Hopkins has perfect reaction to beating alma mater Clemson appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets pulled off a stunning upset of the Clemson Tigers on Saturday, and no one enjoyed it more than wide receivers coach DeAndre Hopkins . Georgia Tech dominated Clemson 20-6 at Memorial Stadium, and Hopkins was all smiles as he celebrated the victory after the game. The moment was made even sweeter by the fact that it came against his alma mater, where he starred as a wide receiver from 2010 to 2012. “It’s happening! It’s about to happen! It’s happening!,” Hopkins said in a clip posted by KingSZN on X, which was originally posted on Instagram. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Georgia Tech WR Coach DeAndre Hopkins celebrating the win over Clemson 😭🔥 Hopkins played WR for Clemson from 2010-2012 (🎥 lamiless on IG) pic.twitter.com/RqCWOvUjcb — KingSZN (@King_Szn10) November 14, 2026 Hopkins joined the Yellow Jackets’ staff in July as an assistant wide receivers coach before being promoted to lead the position group for the final three games of the regular season . Saturday’s trip to Death Valley marked his first game in the new role, and it could not have gone much better. The five-time All-Pro, who spent 13 seasons in the NFL with the Houston Texans, Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans, Kansas City Chiefs and Baltimore Ravens, watched his team control the game from start to finish . Georgia Tech leaned heavily on its ground game, piling up a season-high 269 rushing yards. Justice Haynes led the way with 116 yards, including a 53-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. Grady Adamson added a career-high 87 rushing yards and a score. The Yellow Jackets’ defense was just as impressive, holding Clemson to 228 total yards and keeping the Tigers out of the end zone. Clemson also lost starting quarterback Tait Reynolds to a knee injury on the opening drive. The win was Georgia Tech’s first at Clemson since 2008, snapping an eight-game losing streak at Death Valley. The Yellow Jackets improved to 3-7 on the season, while Clemson fell to 6-4. Georgia Tech will look to carry the momentum into next Saturday’s home game against Wake Forest. top.title: Arch Manning makes a triumphant Louisiana return vs LSU in Week 11
top.description: BATON ROUGE – LSU football found itself in another dogfight against a ranked opponent inside Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. With the Tigers hosting No. 8 Texas in a must-win matchup if they wanted to sniff the College Football Playoff in their first season with Lane Kiffin at the helm, containing the Longhorns star quarterback Arch Manning at the top of the LSU defense's to-do list. For most of the game, it did just that. He threw a season-high three interceptions and it looked like LSU had his number. But in the final two minutes, no one could stand in the way of Manning and victory as he willed Texas to a 22-21 comeback win. He used his legs to bring the Longhorns just shy of the goal line with just 13 seconds left on the clock. And, in a state where his football career started, he made more history, throwing a 4-yard touchdown pass to secure Texas' eighth win of the season. “I think in a bunch of years from now, I’m gonna tell everyone I had a game-winning drive and everyone’s gonna forget the three picks,” Manning joked during his postgame news conference. “I mean, it’s Death Valley at night, 2-minute drive. Let’s go.” Arch Manning never backs down For most of the Week 11 matchup, it was far from the return Manning would’ve hoped for in his first collegiate game in Louisiana. Every pass was contested and any yards gained on the ground were hard fought for Texas’ offense. The Archbishop Newman alum looked rattled to start the game. Before his game-winning 4-yard touchdown pass to Raleek Brown in the final seconds of the game, Manning hadn’t found the end zone at all. “It hadn’t been great all night, so I figured it was time to go get it done,” Manning said. “I grew up around a lot of LSU fans, so it feels good to come back for Mardi Gras or come back whenever I come home and not have them talk a bunch of crap.” Manning remained level-headed in the game despite getting sacked four times. He went on to throw for 174 yards while completing close to 55% of his passes. But this victory wasn’t about Manning looking like the better signal caller. It was all about grit. “It was hard, it was tough and he (Manning) had to use his legs,” Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said. “He got sacked, took some sacks, made some tough throws. But what a drive at the end of the game to shake all that off and to make some of the throws he made. He competed at a really high level tonight. “So I was proud of him, and what a moment for him. Being back in his home state and winning this game the way that it was won.” With this victory, Texas has closed the door for LSU and its dreams for making the College Football Playoffs. For Manning, the win is a little extra sweet as he can join the list of other Mannings who come to Death Valley and left victorious. top.description: Philadelphia Eagles safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. Getty The Philadelphia Eagles wanted out of the C.J. The council described the allegations by the Chairman of the Kano State Multi-Agency Taskforce on Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking, Muhuyi Magaji Rimin-Gado, as baseless and misleading, challenging him to provide verifiable evidence to substantiate his claims. The rebuttal followed allegations made by Rimin-Gado at a press conference in Kano on November 14, where he accused the PCN and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) of allegedly protecting drug dealers operating in the state. nigeria.title: When grandpas, grandmas become cocaine smugglers
nigeria.description: …404 ‘arrested’ in 20 months By Nnamdi Ojiego The image of an elderly grandmother or grandfather being led away by anti-narcotics officers over alleged involvement in drug trafficking is one that challenges conventional perceptions of who participates in the illicit drug trade. Yet, a succession of arrests involving people in their 60s, 70s and even older has brought an uncomfortable question to the fore: Why are people who should ordinarily be enjoying their retirement years becoming involved in the dangerous business of transporting, storing and distributing illicit drugs? In Nigeria, the figures supplied by Femi Babafemi, spokesperson of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) suggest that the phenomenon deserves closer attention. The agency arrested 240 persons aged 60 and above for drug-related offences in 2025, comprising 191 men and 49 women. Between January and August 2026, another 164 elderly suspects, including 128 men and 36 women, were arrested. The figures bring the total number of elderly persons arrested within the 20-month period to 404. Men accounted for the overwhelming majority, representing approximately 80 per cent of the arrests in 2025 and 78 per cent in the first eight months of 2026. Calculated strategy Although the 2026 figures cover only eight months and cannot be directly compared with the full-year 2025 total, the number of arrests already recorded points to the continued involvement of older people in drug-related activities. It also raises questions about the circumstances drawing them into a trade whose consequences include lengthy imprisonment, financial ruin, damaged family relationships and, in some cases, serious health risks. The NDLEA also reported seizing 6,998.77 kilogrammes of illicit drugs in connection with elderly suspects in 2025, compared with 1,479.988 kilogrammes between January and August 2026. From couriers to local dealers The cases recorded by the NDLEA in 2026 provide a glimpse into the different ways older people are becoming involved in the illicit drug trade. On March 14, 2026, NDLEA operatives arrested 74-year-old Ikwuakalom Nwakoro Emeka at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, while he was preparing to board a British Airways flight to London. The agency alleged that 11 kilogrammes of cocaine were discovered in his luggage, concealed in food items, including ground dry pepper. He reportedly told investigators he was travelling to Britain on holiday. Barely three months later, another high-profile case emerged at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos. On June 28, operatives arrested 67-year-old Mary Yetunde Barek, a Nigerian-British woman who worked as a caregiver in the United Kingdom, while she was preparing to board a Virgin Atlantic flight to London. The concerns have been heightened by fresh incidents of political violence in different parts of the country, including Calabar, Cross River State, Asaba, Delta State, and Sokoto, where political supporters and opposition figures have reportedly come under attack. nigeria.description: By Chidi Nkwopara Church leaders have expressed concern over the increasing cases of violent persecution of Christians in parts of Nigeria, saying the disturbing trend has worsened over the past two decades. The Apostolic Nuncio to Nigeria, Archbishop Michael Francis Crotty, and the Archbishop of Owerri, Most Rev. Lucius Iwejuru Ugorji, raised the concern at the weekend in Owerri during their respective addresses at the 18th National Conference of the Association of Papal Knights and Medalists in Nigeria (APKMN). In his address, Crotty said Christians had suffered persecution in different forms throughout Nigeria’s history, but noted that violent forms of persecution had become more pronounced in the last two decades. “In the history of Nigeria, Christians have suffered persecution in different forms, and this disturbing phenomenon has increased within the last two decades, especially the violent forms of persecution. “In recent years, Christians have been targeted by kidnappers, and many lay faithful and priests have been kidnapped. “Many of those kidnapped were killed, and others were released after ransoms were paid. Thousands of churches have been attacked and destroyed since the beginning of Boko Haram and the activities of herdsmen in more recent years,” he said. The Apostolic Nuncio also alleged that Christians in some parts of the country, particularly the North and North-Central regions, had been denied legitimate access to land for the construction of places of worship. “Very often the issue of persecution of Christians in Nigeria is politicised and approached with some sort of bias and religious sentiments. “There is no doubt that people of other faiths have also been affected by insecurity in Nigeria. However, we cannot deny the fact that Christians have been specifically targeted in some parts of the country. “Our concern should be the necessary actions to take in order to bring the unnecessary killing of all citizens to an end, whether they are Christian or of other faiths,” he said. He described the conference theme, “Strategic Engagements in Addressing Christian Persecution in Nigeria: Toward Coordinated Response”, as timely, stressing the need for collective action across religious and community lines. nigeria.description: By Ozioruva Aliu THE governor of Edo, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has said the state already has the structure for state police to commence and for that reason, the state House of Assembly was one of the first to pass the law as recommended by the National Assembly. Okpebholo spoke in an interview with journalists in Benin-City as part of activities to mark his second year anniversary. “We are prepared. We were one of the first to sign into law, when others were talking, we said no, it is working for us and right now, to be honest with you, even with our vigilantes, we already have state police because it is working for us. Edo state is safe.” He said his state already has a working security architecture it has tested that could be used to track criminals even outside the state,” he said. Okpebholo said “Remember there was this kidnapping that happened and within 24 hours which has never happened in Nigeria, we got the guys, so that is it. We are prepared to go to other states when they take any of our citizens. We did it in Kogi, then something happened in Ogun, I called the governor, I said, please, I don’t want my person to stay with this kidnapper for more than five days and as God would have it, he was able to get them out within a short time. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. sports.title: Wild beat Bruins 6-2 behind two goals from Ryan Hartman, extending road winning streak to 8 games
sports.description: Nov 14, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Minnesota Wild left wing Kirill Kaprizov (97) congratulates right wing Ryan Hartman (38) after scoring a goal during the second period against the Boston Bruins at TD Garden. Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect BOSTON — Ryan Hartman and Danila Yurov scored two goals each, Jesper Wallstedt stopped 30 shots, and the Minnesota Wild beat the Boston Bruins 6-2 on Saturday night to extend their road winning streak to eight games. Kirill Kaprizov extended his point streak to 11 games (six goals, 14 assists) with two assists for the West-leading Wild, who have earned at least a point in 11 straight games (9-0-2). Quinn Hughes and Blake Coleman scored 67 seconds apart in the opening two minutes of the second period for Minnesota, which cruised to its NHL-best 10th road victory. Yurov scored both of his in the third period, the second an empty-netter. David Pastrnak and Fraser Minten scored for Boston, which lost its second straight home game after winning seven in a row at TD Garden. Both losses came wearing their new mostly brown “varsity jerseys” with bright yellow numbers, trim and helmets that they debuted Thursday. After getting pulled in Boston’s lopsided loss at home against Montreal Thursday — its first at home since Oct. 5 — Jeremy Swayman started and made 19 saves. Hartman’s first came on a wrister from the left circle that beat Swayman inside the far post, making it 1-0 at 6:54 of the opening period. Hughes slipped a wrister past Swayman 53 seconds into the middle period and Coleman’s slap shot from the point found its way past a few bodies and into the net, making it 3-0. Minten’s power-play goal came at 8:45 but Hartman’s second took away Boston’s brief momentum 75 seconds later. The Wild won the first meeting of the season , 4-1, at home on Oct. 3 when Kaprizov scored two goals. The teams entered tied with the NHL’s second-best goal differential (plus-24) behind Carolina.

Luckily, while college sports were significantly impacted by the sudden travel issues, the Seattle Seahawks were able to head to Las Vegas to take on the Raiders as originally scheduled. The Seahawks are en route to Las Vegas right now as planned, so no changes to their travel schedule. — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) November 14, 2026 It sure helps to have a charter flight in this scenario. The NFL is probably fortunate that not a single Week 10 Sunday matchup has a Pacific Time Zone team playing in the Eastern Time Zone (or vice versa). College football and basketball games were rescheduled throughout the country as a result of Friday’s outage, with the Washington Huskies men’s basketball matchup with Utah postponed outright to December due to additional travel problems . Huskies football did fly to Michigan on Friday night but still had their kickoff against Michigan State moved back by an hour. The NFL didn’t come away from the travel nightmare unscathed, as several games will have makeshift officiating crews. A playing career that had so much promise would drift into relative obscurity after his time at Chelsea and Tottenham in the 90s, and he was even forced into early retirement. Now, though, he is going viral across social media on a near-weekly basis for his on-air antics. Cundy is a talkSPORT stalwart after more than 20 years with the radio station, but his emergence as a master wind-up merchant has seen his popularity soar. In fact, the 56-year-old's 'generational run' means there there is an argument he should be sweeping sports broadcasting awards in 2026. Chelsea, survival & early retirement Cundy started his career at Chelsea before going on to play for Tottenham, but his playing days were hampered by a series of health problems While he is now arguably more synonymous with being a broadcaster after more than 20 years in the business, Cundy actually enjoyed a top-level professional playing career that incorporated spells at Chelsea and, ironically, their London rivals Tottenham, whom he now spends a significant chunk of his time tearing into. A lifelong Chelsea fan who used to watch the Blues at Stamford Bridge as a boy, the tough-tackling centre-back came through the club's academy in the 80s, earning their Young Player of the Year award in 1987. He spent four years in the first team in west London before being sold to Spurs in 1992. Hampered by persistent fitness issues throughout his career, Cundy was forced to be patient for opportunities at White Hart Lane and headed on various loans before permanent spells with Ipswich Town and Portsmouth. It was during his time with the latter that the defender was diagnosed with testicular cancer in early 1997, undergoing surgery to remove one of his testicles and eventually making a full recovery, returning to the pitch later that year. sports.description: Bundesliga defender not a viable option for Barcelona despite recent links – report Last week, it was reported that Jonathan Tah has emerged as a potential candidate for Barcelona as they look to shore up their ranks in the defensive unit in January. The club have struggled with injuries in the defensive department, with the likes of Eric Garcia, Andreas Christensen, Jules Kounde, and Xavi Espart all picking up injuries at some form or the other. This has led Barcelona to reportedly consider a move for Bayern Munich star Tah, who is a key defender for both his club and country. Tah not an option for Barcelona Jonathan Tah is a key player for German national team. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) However, a recent report from Diario SPORT has now clarified that Tah is not a serious option for Barcelona. This is largely because Bayern Munich are not willing to consider the sale of the German international, while the player himself is not too keen on leaving the club either. Therefore, a Barcelona move for Tah has been practically ruled out, even though the club are interested in acquiring the services of the former Bayer Leverkusen star. It must be noted that Barça were one of the contenders to sign Tah when he had decided to run out his contract at Leverkusen in 2025. Ultimately, Bayern Munich won the race to his signature. No change of air required Tah believes Bayern is the place to be. (Photo by Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images) The report points out that Barcelona do have an excellent relationship with Tah’s agent, Pini Zahavi. The Israeli agent is the representative of Hansi Flick and shares a good bond with Joan Laporta, having previously helped the club sign Robert Lewandowski as well. However, Tah is simply not willing to leave Bayern Munich, having already established himself as a key player at the back, with 67 appearances in all competitions since joining the club. Now a regular in the German team as well, Tah is currently at the peak of his powers and believes Bayern is the place to be. sports.title: Arch Manning makes a triumphant Louisiana return vs LSU in Week 11
sports.description: BATON ROUGE – LSU football found itself in another dogfight against a ranked opponent inside Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. With the Tigers hosting No. 8 Texas in a must-win matchup if they wanted to sniff the College Football Playoff in their first season with Lane Kiffin at the helm, containing the Longhorns star quarterback Arch Manning at the top of the LSU defense's to-do list. For most of the game, it did just that. He threw a season-high three interceptions and it looked like LSU had his number. But in the final two minutes, no one could stand in the way of Manning and victory as he willed Texas to a 22-21 comeback win. He used his legs to bring the Longhorns just shy of the goal line with just 13 seconds left on the clock. And, in a state where his football career started, he made more history, throwing a 4-yard touchdown pass to secure Texas' eighth win of the season. “I think in a bunch of years from now, I’m gonna tell everyone I had a game-winning drive and everyone’s gonna forget the three picks,” Manning joked during his postgame news conference. “I mean, it’s Death Valley at night, 2-minute drive. Let’s go.” Arch Manning never backs down For most of the Week 11 matchup, it was far from the return Manning would’ve hoped for in his first collegiate game in Louisiana. Every pass was contested and any yards gained on the ground were hard fought for Texas’ offense. The Archbishop Newman alum looked rattled to start the game. Before his game-winning 4-yard touchdown pass to Raleek Brown in the final seconds of the game, Manning hadn’t found the end zone at all. “It hadn’t been great all night, so I figured it was time to go get it done,” Manning said. “I grew up around a lot of LSU fans, so it feels good to come back for Mardi Gras or come back whenever I come home and not have them talk a bunch of crap.” Manning remained level-headed in the game despite getting sacked four times. He went on to throw for 174 yards while completing close to 55% of his passes. But this victory wasn’t about Manning looking like the better signal caller. It was all about grit. “It was hard, it was tough and he (Manning) had to use his legs,” Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said. “He got sacked, took some sacks, made some tough throws. But what a drive at the end of the game to shake all that off and to make some of the throws he made. He competed at a really high level tonight. “So I was proud of him, and what a moment for him. Being back in his home state and winning this game the way that it was won.” With this victory, Texas has closed the door for LSU and its dreams for making the College Football Playoffs. For Manning, the win is a little extra sweet as he can join the list of other Mannings who come to Death Valley and left victorious. sports.description: UNLV Rebels quarterback Jackson Arnold (11) scrambles during a game against the New Mexico Lobos at University Stadium in Albuquerque, NM, on Nov. 14, 2026. ALBUQUERQUE—The UNLV Rebels might not have had the season expected of a Mountain West favorite, but they had zero issue playing the role of College Football Playoff spoiler. On Saturday, UNLV put together one of their most inspired efforts of the season, surprising the current Mountain West leading New Mexico Lobos 21-14 to all but dash the conference’s hopes of landing the Group of 6 CFP berth. It was far from smooth sailing for UNLV, however, as they had expected difficulties against one of the best defenses in the nation. Quarterback Jackson Arnold only had 49 passing yards in the first half and was subbed out for Alex Orji on occasion. He was also responsible for two turnovers in New Mexico territory, as UNLV sputtered to only seven points through three quarters. However, with the Rebels down 14 at the end of the third quarter, Arnold and the offense came alive at a crucial time. After the defense forced New Mexico to punt on Arnold’s second turnover, he would lead an efficient drive downfield, ending with a 43-yard touchdown pass to Kayden McGee to cut the lead down to one possession. On the next drive, Arnold would secure another big play on a 44-yard touchdown run to give UNLV their first lead of the game with seven and a half minutes to go. However, the Rebels would need their defense to come up large, and the maligned unit put together a quality effort. While the Rebels did allow 203 rushing yards to continue the struggles against the run, they were able to take advantage of a Lobos team down on its luck at the quarterback position. Linebacker Cam Santee was responsible for one of three sacks, as well as leading the Rebels with 12 tackles (2.5 for loss). Andre Porter and Elias Rudolph recorded the other sacks. However, UNLV’s biggest play would come on the final New Mexico drive, as cornerback Tony-Louis Nkuba was able to record the game-winning interception for their sole turnover of the game. With their sixth victory on the season, the Rebels secured bowl eligibility for the fourth consecutive season, which becomes a new program record. UNLV now has a chance to secure some real momentum heading into their bowl game, finishing off their road schedule against San Jose State next Saturday.

science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide on everything you need to observe and photograph the planets of the solar system, along with our picks of the top telescopes , cameras and lenses for exploring the night sky in 2026. science.title: New Scientist readers on how the magazine has shaped their lives
science.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick. Frank Eva

science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. All went according to plan after that for Ship as well: A second engine burn lasting about 20 seconds parked Ship in LEO at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) at T+26 minutes and 10 seconds. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28. Ship carried 26 of SpaceX's Starlink V3 spacecraft, which were deployed into LEO on schedule today over a 42-minute span starting 35 minutes after launch. The upgraded wireless internet satellites are the second V3 batch to reach orbit, after a set of 26 that were delivered on Flight 14 . V3s are significantly more powerful than SpaceX's V2 Starlinks, which currently number more than 11,000 in LEO. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans. science.title: 100 launches! Rocket Lab sends Earth-observing satellite to orbit on milestone mission (photos)
science.description: null Rocket Lab just hit the century mark. An Electron rocket topped with a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite lifted off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site on Saturday (Nov. 14) at 12:30 a.m. EST (0530 GMT; 6:30 p.m. local New Zealand time). The mission, which Rocket Lab called "The Mountain God Rises," was a big one: It marked the 100th launch to date for the California-based company. The first stage of Rocket Lab's Electron rocket falls back to Earth during "The Mountain God Rises" mission on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) Rocket Lab launched for the first time in May 2017, sending the brand-new Electron up on a test flight from New Zealand. That effort failed, but Electron bounced back on its second-ever liftoff, delivering several cubesats to low Earth orbit (LEO) in January 2018. In the years since, the 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron has become one of the most prolific and reliable rockets in the world, carrying small payloads to the final frontier for a variety of customers. And it hit the century mark on Saturday in record-breaking fashion: No commercially developed rocket has gotten there faster, not even SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 , according to Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck. "It's an unprecedented milestone for a commercial small-lift orbital rocket, and a threshold rarely crossed in modern spaceflight," Beck said on Monday (Nov. 9), during Rocket Lab's third-quarter earnings call with investors. "But what matters most to us and our customers is that we have achieved a 96% reliability rate across 99 launches." Electron met the moment in style on Saturday morning, thanks to some fancy livery. "Black rocket 🤝 Golden milestone. Electron is all dressed up for launch 100," Rocket Lab said via X on Tuesday (Nov. 10), in a post that shared a photo of the specially painted first stage. Not all of Rocket Lab's missions have gone orbital, it should be noted: A suborbital variant of Electron known as HASTE , which customers use to test technologies in a hypersonic flight environment, has nine missions under its belt to date. The Electron rocket that flew Rocket Lab's 100th mission sported some special livery. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) "The Mountain God Rises" was Rocket Lab's 11th launch to date for the Tokyo-based company iQPS, which is building a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in LEO. And all went to plan on the mission: Electron's upper "kick stage" deployed a single iQPS spacecraft 357 miles (575 kilometers) above Earth. SAR satellites can see through cloud cover and image our planet at night as well as during the day, offering key advantages over spacecraft that are optimized to view in optical wavelengths. science.title: California's brand-new Air & Space Center, home of the space shuttle Endeavour, opens today
science.description: null LOS ANGELES — The California Science Center officially opened its brand-new Samuel Oschin Air & Space Center to the public today (Nov. 13). After more than three decades in development, folks can finally visit the Los Angeles science museum's massive new wing. For most of us, the biggest draw is its centerpiece: the retired space shuttle Endeavour , sitting upright in launch position, towering at nearly 200 feet (61 meters) tall. "It just takes your breath away when you see that reveal and the doors open and you get to look at it for the first time. It's just — it's overwhelming," former NASA astronaut Garrett Reisman told Space.com during a visit to the museum. Reisman flew on two space shuttle missions during his astronaut career, the first of which was on Endeavour. The space shuttle Endeavour. (Image credit: Olivia Hemaratanatorn/Future) "There are people that come from all over the world, and when they come to Los Angeles, they're going to have the opportunity to see it, too," Reisman added. "The exposure it's going to have is just a force multiplier. There are so many people that can have that opportunity to bring their kids here and show them [the shuttle] and have that experience." Entering into this exhibit is an experience in and of itself, as I can personally attest; I was among of group of reporters who got a sneak peek at the new wing on Oct. 28. A video presentation ends in a dramatic reveal: Visitors walk into a space where the enormous shuttle, which flew 25 missions to Earth orbit from 1992 to 2011, feels truly larger than life. The new Endeavour exhibit features a replica launch tower, from which you can look down at the shuttle. (Image credit: Future) There are a number of interactive exhibits around the base of Endeavour, which you can slide down to (though, of course, you can also take the elevator or stairs). From a shuttle landing simulator to a replica of a shuttle cockpit that you can sit in, to shuttle tires and space tech from across decades of spaceflight history, there's an incredible variety of space artifacts to both observe and interact with. As for Endeavour itself: It is open, so you can peer inside to see the robotic arm tucked away among a myriad of handles, straps and electronic gear inside. And you can see the shuttle from underneath all the way to the top. A replica of the space shuttle Endeavour's flight deck. (Image credit: Olivia Hemaratanatorn/Future) You can lie on the floor underneath the shuttle's engines, for example, and then take an elevator up the launch tower to come face-to-face with Endeavour's nose. There's even a transparent floor at the top that allows you to stand above the shuttle (though if you have a fear of heights, this might not be for you). science.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
science.description: null Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars. In fact, you're likely to catch their collective brightness in your peripheral vision every time you go outside and look up. But every November the Pleiades remind me that naked-eye observing isn't as simple as opening the back door and looking up. How many Pleiades I can see can change depending on what I do during the next 10 minutes. What's happening and when to look You can easily see the Pleiades as a bright misty patch in your peripheral vision during winter. (Image credit: Haitong Yu via Getty Images) The Pleiades, also known as Messier 45 (M45) or the "Seven Sisters," are an open star cluster in Taurus. They're one of the closest clusters to the solar system and some of the youngest stars you can see with the naked eye — just 100 million years old. They're basically newborns. In mid-November, they rise in the east in the early evening and climb higher as the night progresses, making this an excellent time to get acquainted with them. Look east after dark for a tiny, compact group of stars. If you know Orion, which rises later, the Pleiades are above and to the right of it from mid-northern latitudes. Nearby you'll also find orange Aldebaran and the much broader V-shaped Hyades cluster. The Hyades are closer to the sun , but their stars are about 625 million years old. The name "Seven Sisters" creates an immediate observational trap: people assume they're supposed to see seven stars. That's not necessarily true. In fact, six is a common naked-eye result under decently dark conditions (note that the shape of the six brightest is like a mini Big Dipper /Plough), while people with sharp eyesight under darker skies may see more. The cluster itself contains about 1,000 stars. The number you personally distinguish depends on eyesight, sky brightness, atmospheric conditions and how well your eyes have adapted to darkness. That makes M45 much more interesting to me than a simple tick-box target. So tonight, don't just find the Pleiades — count them. science.title: 'Martian Isolation' is an upcoming sci-fi survival horror game that looks like 'The Martian' and 'Event Horizon' had a horrific child
science.description: null "Martian Isolation" is an upcoming single-player, first-person survival horror game that's just been revealed with a suitably creepy launch trailer. And yes, it does look an awful lot like " The Martian ," doesn't it? There's a lot of survival gameplay on display here that mirrors Mark Watney's tale of survival on the Red Planet, as your stranded protagonist is forced to explore the Martian surface to acquire resources, grow plants, and repair their base. That comparison to Andy Weir's sci-fi masterpiece does fall away as you get further into the trailer, though, when the horror part of the game's description comes into play: Flickering lights, creepy figures stalking the halls of your Martian habitat, and blood dripping from the walls. Oh yeah, that's some good creepy sci-fi horror right there. It's giving " Event Horizon ", and that's always getting a thumbs-up from me. There's no release date scheduled at this time, with the 'Martian Isolation' Steam page simply listing it as "coming soon," though the YouTube trailer description does say it "will be available on Steam in 2027". You can't pre-order yet, but if this looks like your jam, you can add it to your wishlist. Beyond that, we know shockingly little about this title. It's the debut game from Golden Milestone Studio, but there's very little information out there beyond a name. The latest blog post on the game's Steam page says that they're a "small team," but what we've seen so far is encouraging. There seems to be a pronounced split between the survival and horror elements of the game along the day/night cycle. Daytime sees you exploring the Martian surface, smashing rocks, cleaning solar panels, and doing sick jumps on a quad bike. The psychological torment only begins once the sun goes down (they mostly come out at night … mostly), as your character starts encountering cosmic horrors and weird naked zombie men. Mars rover, nice. Golden Milestone Studio Spacesuits, check. Golden Milestone Studio Crafting, of course. Golden Milestone Studio OH SWEET JESUS! Get it away, get it away. Golden Milestone Studio OK, we're good. Mining, cool. Golden Milestone Studio Riding a quad bike on Mars, yes please. Golden Milestone Studio Growing potatoes on Mars, just like that guy in the movie. Golden Milestone Studio Opening a box with power tools, seems excessive but sure. Golden Milestone Studio NOPE! Nope, nope, nope, I'm out! Golden Milestone Studio Are they hallucinations, or is there some malevolent presence hiding in the blood-red sands of Mars ? I'm always looking for new ways to shatter my psyche and possibly soil my pants, so I'll be keeping a close eye on this one. In the meantime, I do need to get back and finish " Routine ." I left my character hiding under a desk months ago, and I haven't been brave enough to go back. As Mama always said, you can't have any Martian horror until you finish your lunar horror first.
